lines.trans: Thank you very much for selecting me.

words.t: ありがとうございます
words.reading: アリガトウゴザイマス

lines.trans: Please never forget that sense of shyness.
Good morning. You all look wonderful.
Ms. Kuroki, it is an honor to meet you.
The honor is mine as well. I look forward to working with you.
Now then! Let's change the world through erotica.
Keep polishing yourselves. You may spend as much as you like to do that.
What I am putting the most effort into is without a doubt our exclusive actresses.

words.gram: Plain imperative form of 入る (to enter).

lines.trans: They won their way through a rigorous audition out of ten thousand applicants.
They are the luckiest women in Japan.
We will create the brilliance of a hundred-million-carat diamond.
Is everyone ready? Face the cameras and give your very best smiles.
Thank you very much for selecting me.

examples.text: 選んでくださり、ありがとうございます。
examples.trans: Thank you very much for selecting me.

examples.text: あら、じゃあわたくしのも選んでいただこうかしら。広告のお仕事がありますの。
examples.trans: Oh my, then perhaps I'll ask you to pick something for me too. I have an ad shoot coming up.

meanings.note: Plain sentence-ending copula; contracts or shifts to だった in past, だろう/だろ for supposition, and で/じゃ in combinations.
All-purpose action verb; turns Sino-Japanese nouns into verbs (融通する, 出店する) and with に means 'decide on' or 'make into'.

examples.text: お前ら、観光じゃないんだからしっかりしろよ。
examples.trans: Hey, this isn't sightseeing, so pull yourselves together.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.note: Standalone casual thanks; followed by ございます (present) or ございました (completed occasion) for polite thanks.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。

meanings.en: that (near the listener or just mentioned)
meanings.note: Must always precede a noun (その椅子 'that chair').
Derived from the verb 恥じる (to feel shy/ashamed).

examples.text: 彼女には恥じらいがある。
examples.trans: She has a sense of modesty.

meanings.note: Written を and pronounced o; marks what an action directly acts upon.
Negates verbs or forms じゃない ('is not') in questions like いいんじゃないか.

meanings.en: location of action; means; scope total
meanings.note: Marks where an action happens, the unit/scope of a rate or total (十日で, 全部で), or the cause/occasion.

examples.trans: It is one thousand yen in total.

meanings.note: Follows a verb's て-form or polite お + stem (お待ちください, お持ち帰りください) to make a polite request.

examples.text: ここに書いてください。

meanings.note: Polite form is おはようございます.

examples.trans: Good morning, did you sleep well?

examples.text: みんなにおはようと言う。

meanings.en: polite auxiliary in ありがとうございます
meanings.note: Survives in modern speech chiefly in ございます (present) and ございました (past) after ありがとう and おめでとう.

examples.text: ありがとうございます。
ありがとうございました。
examples.trans: Thank you very much (for what just concluded).

meanings.note: Polite way to address a group of people.

examples.text: 皆さんにお知らせがあります。
examples.trans: I have an announcement for everyone.

examples.text: おはようございます。皆さんステキですわ。
examples.trans: Good morning. You all look wonderful.

examples.text: ホントにステキなセンスですね。どうしてお仕事お辞めになられたんですか？
examples.trans: You truly have lovely taste. Why did you leave your job?

meanings.note: Polite sentence-ending counterpart of plain だ.

cells: ではありません / じゃありません

meanings.note: Attached to surnames, given names, or company names to show everyday respect; never used for oneself.
Prefixed to native Japanese words (お店, お二人, お持ち帰り) to add politeness.
Polite volitional 会いましょう in また会いましょう means 'let us meet again'.

examples.trans: I meet a friend at the station.

examples.text: また来週会いましょう。

できる.gloss: be built; open; be able to

meanings.en: come into existence; be completed; can do
meanings.note: With buildings or stores (店ができる), means a new shop has been built or opened.

examples.text: 駅前に新しいカフェができました。
examples.trans: A new café opened in front of the station.

examples.text: 日本語が少しできます。
examples.trans: I can speak a little Japanese.

examples.text: 黒木さん、お会いできて光栄です。
examples.trans: Ms. Kuroki, it is an honor to meet you.

examples.text: こちらこそ光栄ですわ。よろしくお願いいたします。
examples.trans: The honor is mine as well. I look forward to working with you.

meanings.note: Core adverb in set greetings like よろしくお願いします and どうぞよろしく.
With します, forms お願いします ('please'), the standard polite way to request a service or favor.

examples.text: 一つお願いがあります。
examples.trans: I have one favor to ask.

meanings.note: Humble (kenjougo) equivalent of する, used in polite business and apologetic expressions.

examples.text: すぐにご連絡いたします。
examples.trans: I will contact you right away.

meanings.note: Prompts someone into action or shoos them along.
Used for the physical world or a specific sphere/industry (この世界).

examples.text: この世界に入る覚悟はあるか。
examples.trans: Are you prepared to enter this world?

meanings.note: Tells the listener something new or adds warm reassurance at the end of a sentence.
Reflexive pronoun pointing back to the person under discussion.

examples.text: 自分の言葉で話します。
examples.trans: I speak in my own words.

examples.text: どんどん自分を磨いてください。そのためにはいくら使ってもかまいません。
examples.trans: Keep polishing yourselves. You may spend as much as you like to do that.

examples.text: 現場でよく聞く言葉だ。
examples.trans: It's an expression often heard on set.

meanings.en: target, location of existence, or result marker
meanings.note: Marks destination, location where something exists or sits, or the chosen result before する and なる.
Used both to answer yes politely and when handing an item to someone.
Attaches to pronouns or people nouns (僕ら, 彼ら).
Godan verb.

examples.text: このペンを使ってもいいですか。
もっと英語を使いましょう。

meanings.note: Replaces は, が, or を to add 'also' or 'too'.

examples.trans: Please give me this one too.

examples.text: あそこも新しい店です。
examples.trans: Over there is a new shop too.

meanings.note: Turns a statement into a question, or softens a volitional/negative guess.
Polite/dialectal negative ending, especially in ～ません.
Before an adjective (一番近い), forms the superlative ('closest').

examples.trans: This one is the most popular.

examples.text: 一番近い駅はどこですか。

meanings.note: Godan verb: potential polite 入れます (はいれます) means 'can enter'.

examples.text: 予約なしでも入れますか。
examples.trans: Can we get in without a reservation?

meanings.note: Marks the presence of a person (責任者はいるか) or follows て-form (often contracted to てる/てます in speech).
Refers to facts, matters, or affairs rather than physical objects (もの).

examples.text: 仕事のことを話します。

meanings.en: as for; topic or contrast marker
meanings.note: Written は but pronounced wa when marking the topic or contrasting one item with another.

examples.text: 一番力を入れていることは、間違いなく専属女優たちです。
examples.trans: What I am putting the most effort into is without a doubt our exclusive actresses.

meanings.note: Links a modifying noun to a following noun, or turns a clause into an explanatory statement (often contracted to ん in speech).
Follows a clause to give a reason or reassuring explanation.

examples.trans: Because it is close, I walk.

meanings.en: casual reflection or firm reminder particle
meanings.note: Used aloud to oneself ('man, I'm hungry') or at the end of a warning ('remember that, okay?').
Standard gender-neutral 'I' in polite and business Japanese.
Marks the subject of existence, emergence, or questions (どれが), and at the end of a polite clause softens a request (のですが).

examples.text: お願いがあるのですが。
examples.trans: I have a favor to ask.

meanings.note: Subsidiary ichidan verb written in hiragana after て-form (～てみる).

examples.text: 一度食べてみてください。
やってみなければ分かりません。
examples.trans: You won't know unless you try.

meanings.en: open a store; bring out; hand in
meanings.note: 店を出す means opening a branch; 出しやがって attaches tough-guy disdainful やがる.

examples.text: 駅前に新しい店を出します。
examples.trans: We open a new branch in front of the station.

examples.text: 書類を出してください。

meanings.note: Conjunctive particle giving a reason, softer than から.

examples.text: 雨が降っているので、家にいます。
examples.trans: Since it's raining, I'm staying home.

examples.text: 時間がないので急ぎましょう。
examples.trans: We don't have time, so let's hurry.

meanings.note: Irregular i-adjective whose past/conditional stems use よ- (よかったら).

examples.text: よかったら来てください。
皆さんいいですか？カメラに向かって最高の笑顔でいきますよ。
examples.trans: Is everyone ready? Face the cameras and give your very best smiles.

examples.text: お世話になっております。今ちょうど向かっていますよ。
examples.trans: Thank you for everything. We are on our way right now.

examples.text: リムジン八台に女優、男優、助監督を乗せてスタート地点へ向かう。
examples.trans: Eight limousines carrying actresses, actors, and assistant directors will head to the starting line.

meanings.note: Noun.

examples.text: 彼女はいつも笑顔が素敵だ。
examples.trans: She always has a lovely smile.

examples.text: 笑顔で挨拶しましょう。
examples.trans: Let's greet people with a smile.

meanings.en: go forward; work out well (いけます = 'it will work!')
meanings.note: Written in kana for figurative headway: いけます! ('this can go / this will work!'), 思いどおりにいかない ('does not go as hoped').

examples.text: この企画ならいけます！
examples.trans: With this plan, it will work!

examples.text: 仕事がうまくいっています。

meanings.note: Used in everyday farewells like またね, また明日, and また会いましょう.

examples.text: また明日会いましょう。
